comment: Short reference runs (~30s each). Each must stay bit-identical across every refactor step. NB: windows shorter than ~60 interventions crash in reinforcement_returning (lookup runs past the end of the sliced df_pc), so --end must stay comfortably above that. The same lookup in reinforcement_sending sets a *data-dependent* floor: it reads the num_inter of the first event at or after the reinforcement's arrival time, so a run whose last reinforcement lands past the slice raises IndexError. That floor rises with firefighter availability (more crews available means more reinforcements sent), which is why heuristic_best_ff1 needs a longer window than the ff3 cases: it crashes at --end 400 and 600, and runs at 800.

cases.comment: --end 800, not 400: with full firefighter availability this case sends a reinforcement whose arrival falls past a 400- or 600-event slice, and reinforcement_sending then indexes an empty result. 800 clears it.
cases.name: heuristic_best_ff1

cases.comment: --end 800 for the same reason as heuristic_best_ff1: a reinforcement arrives past a 400-event slice and reinforcement_sending indexes an empty result.
cases.name: heuristic_best_veh3

cases.comment: FQF agent, train mode from a fresh seeded init (no checkpoint exists for the current agent API). Weights are only saved every 10000 interventions, so a short run writes none. device=cpu in the fixture: GPU kernels are not bit-reproducible. capture_metrics because the script accepts --save_metrics_as but never writes it.
cases.name: agent_fqf_train
